text:
hope: Bringing up Tessera-9B from vendor X. Tokenizer appears Llama-ish but there's an odd high-id sentinel (65535) that decodes to a private-use glyph (\uE000). Could be a placeholder insertion during export. Anyone run into 65535 before? :eyes:

raj: can you share a tiny repro? especially encode/decode and a small slice of the vocab file so we can see ordering.

hope: quick REPL dump: 
```
>>> tokenizer.encode("Test — newline")
[1212, 65535, 44, 2]
>>> tokenizer.decode([1212, 65535, 44, 2])
"Test \uE000 newline"
```
After 65535 ids look shifted relative to our embedding table.

marta: that id really screams "vendor sentinel". Two things to watch: 1) kv-cache offsets (if we blindly shift IDs embedding->kv ordering breaks) 2) rotary freq/base expectations. Vendor metadata shows rotary_base: 12000 which differs from our 8192 pipeline. Phase drift across heads will cause subtle ranking/regression.

ciara: FYI I pushed a quick quant run (gptq-int4, default blocksize) on the raw checkpoint: 
- SummEval ROUGE-L: -3.1% vs fp16 baseline 
- Perplexity on C4: +0.9 ppl (negligible)
- MMLU: -0.2%
So generation-quality drop concentrated on summarization.

eval-bot: staging run summary: {"model":"tessera9b-gptq-int4","summ_eval_rouge_l":"-3.1%","ppl_delta":"+0.9","tokens":"95k"}

hope: thinking aloud: easiest immediate remediation is an alias at tokenization time mapping 65535 -> existing BOS/EOS (id 3 in this model) so downstream indices align. Also add a sparse remap in the embedding lookup to avoid shifting all embeddings. Example: 
```python
# alias map applied before embedding lookup
alias = {65535: 3}

def apply_alias(ids):
    return [alias.get(i, i) for i in ids]

# sparse remap: copy embedding row for new id into slot 3 if present
if 65535 < model.vocab_size:
    emb[3] = emb[65535]  # sparse operation, only if sentinel exists in checkpoint
```
This keeps the vocab_size stable and avoids touching downstream weight ordering.

raj: agree on alias + sparse remap. For rotary, small headwise check after rescale helps validate. Marta, do you have a quick scaling patch?

marta: yes — rough patch: 
```python
# normalize rotary frequencies to our runtime base
rotary_base = model.config.get('rotary_base', 8192)
if rotary_base != 8192:
    scale = 8192.0 / float(rotary_base)
    model.rotary.inv_freq *= scale
    # recompute sin/cos caches if precomputed
```
Ran the check on a handful of positions and head dims: max abs diff in attention logits vs fp16 < 2e-4 after rescale.

ciara: will wire alias + rotary-rescale into a temporary conversion hook and re-run the gptq pipeline tonight. Also adding a targeted summarization eval set to catch that ROUGE drop.

merge-bot: CI note: scheduling long-run for tessera9b conversion + eval on staging-pool at 02:00 UTC (expected ~7h). Patch branch: feat/tessera-sentinel-alias.

hope: quick note for model-convert: we should persist an id_alias.json alongside the converted model when any nontrivial aliasing happens. That way downstream code knows there was a rename.

raj: +1 to id_alias.json. Also add a unit test that token_id roundtrips: encode->alias->embed_lookup->decode to ensure we don't silently change text roundtrips.

marta: one more check: ensure max(token_id) < saved_vocab_size after conversion. If vendor adds sentinel>vocab_size, conversion should either drop or remap but never offset the whole table.

hope: thanks team. I'll drop the conversion hook PR and tag you all. Will post eval diffs tomorrow morning. :rocket:
